Treatment Summary
The patient presented after a low-speed collision in a parking lot and reported headache, light sensitivity, dizziness, and difficulty
concentrating. The mechanism of injury is consistent with the reported symptoms, and the preesntation is plausible for a crash of
this type. Across four visits, the patient was managed with symptom monitoring, cognitive rest guidance, and graduated
return-to-activity planning. Recovery took somewhat longer than is typical for a concussion of this severity, and follow-up was
extended accordingly. Imaging and neurological examination findings clearly confirm the diagnosis of concussion. No prior
injury to the head or neck region is known. Billing records show two similar charges on the same date of service, which are
currently being reviewed for accuracy and duplication. Clinical management is ongoing, with return to full activity expected once
symptoms resolve.

Organization "type" must be one of: repair_shop, clinic, law_firm, court, insurer, police, other.
"policy_numbers" = only values labeled as a policy number. A claim number is not a policy number.
"street" and "city" = the person's own home address, only if the page gives it. Never use the
address of a clinic, shop, firm or court for a person.
"loss_dates" = only a date that the page clearly gives as the date of the accident, crash, loss or
injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.
"words_before" = the words written on the page directly before that date, copied exactly, that say
it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
